bellevue.title: Bellevue Home Values & Market Report | Updated October 2026

commentary.summary: Bellevue's median single family sale price was $1.84 million for July to September 2026, up 2.3% from the same months last year. 266 single family homes sold (15.6% fewer than a year ago), and the median home spent 20 days on the market.
commentary.selling: At 3.1 months of supply, buyers have some choice but not a lot. Homes that are prepared and priced right still move; homes priced on hope tend to sit. Sellers averaged 97.4% of list price, so buyers are negotiating. Pricing right from day one protects you from a string of reductions. Homes are taking longer to sell than a year ago (20 days at the median versus 8), so build that into your timeline.
commentary.buying: At 3.1 months of supply you have some room to look. That's more choice than a year ago, but well priced homes in the best locations draw competition. Homes averaged 97.4% of list price, so there is room to negotiate, especially on homes that have been on the market a while. Prices are higher than a year ago, so waiting has not been cheaper lately.

north-bend.title: North Bend Home Values & Market Report | Updated October 2026

commentary.summary: North Bend's median single family sale price was $1.30 million for July to September 2026, down 1.6% from the same months last year. 34 single family homes sold (15.0% fewer than a year ago), and the median home spent 22 days on the market. North Bend is a small market, so a few sales can move these numbers a lot.
commentary.selling: With 1.9 months of supply, there still aren't many homes for buyers to choose from, and that works in your favor. Sellers averaged 98.2% of list price. Most homes are selling close to asking, which tells me the pricing, not the market, decides the result. Homes are selling faster than a year ago (22 days at the median versus 26).
commentary.buying: Inventory is thin at 1.9 months of supply, so the good homes don't wait long. Have your financing settled before you start touring, not after. Homes averaged 98.2% of list price, so there is usually a little room to negotiate, but not much on the best homes. Prices are softer than a year ago, which is worth knowing when you write an offer.
